item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Monday
item.description: Slight rise for property prices, first month without fatal shooting in eight years, all of Sweden below freezing for first time this winter and more news from Sweden on Monday.

item.title: Northvolt lost ten months due to gamble with untested Chinese machines
item.description: Swedish battery company Northvolt gambled on bringing in untested machines from China and ended up losing at least 10 months as a result, the Dagens Nyheter newspaper has reported on the basis of documents held by the bankruptcy administrator.

item.title: Lawyer says Sweden's plan to revoke residencies 'illegal on multiple counts'
item.description: There are so many reasons why Sweden's proposed law to revoke existing permanent residencies would be illegal that it's hard to believe those pushing it seriously intend it to happen, immigration lawyer Tomas Fridh tells The Local.

item.title: Why the Swedish krona’s rise might be nearing its end
item.description: The US dollar has dropped in value while the Swedish krona has risen in recent months, but forecasts from a number of banks predict the krona might have reached a plateau.

item.title: Sweden to pass twelve new migration laws before September election
item.description: In an interview with Svenska Dagbladet (SvD), Swedish Migration Minister Johan Forssell has said he plans to pass twelve new migration laws in what he calls “the largest ever change in migration policy”.

item.title: EU 'monitoring' Sweden's plan to revoke permanent residency permits
item.description: The EU's migration commissioner has said he is monitoring Sweden's plan to revoke existing permanent residency permits and is ready to step in if Sweden pushes ahead with it in a way which contravenes EU law, adding yet another obstacle to what is arguably the government's most controversial migration proposal.

item.title: Swedish word of the day: galen
item.description: Here's a word that's fairly common in Swedish and has a fascinating history, but be careful how you use it.

item.title: EU says countries can halt EES checks over summer to avoid travel chaos
item.description: Member States will have the green light to partially suspend Europe's Entry/Exit System (EES), the new EU digital border system, over the summer to avoid any travel chaos at ports and airports during peak season.

item.title: Why does Sweden's government want a new list of jobs exempted from the salary limit?
item.description: Sweden's government last week ordered the Migration Agency to produce another list of professions to exempted from the new, higher salary threshold for a work permit, barely six months after ordering a similar list. Why is it ordering another one and how will it be different?

item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Tuesday
item.description: Court to rule on Swedish citizens behind Denmark grenade attack, government to abolish F grade, migration minister to apply 'poor conduct' law retroactively and more news from Sweden on Tuesday.
